assertions.text: Output contains a @TableTest annotation
assertions.evidence: Found @TableTest annotation

assertions.text: Each policy threshold (650 for non-seniors, 600 for seniors) is verifiable from the table...
assertions.evidence: Rows 'At the standard threshold...650...REJECTED' and 'Just above...651...APPROVED'; also 600/601 pair for seniors

assertions.text: Cell values use concrete domain terms...
assertions.evidence: 40 | 650 | true | REJECTED and 70 | 601 | true | APPROVED — concrete numbers/enums, boolean for income

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: First column(s): "Scenario"

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions, not outcomes.
assertions.evidence: 'Below threshold rejects regardless of stable income' and 'Below threshold rejects even with missing income info' embed the outcome verb 'rejects'

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language.
assertions.evidence: Header row: 'Scenario | Age | Credit Score | Stable Income | Result?'

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Decision?' or 'Status?')
assertions.evidence: Question-mark columns: Result?

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: 1 method(s) checked — no if/switch/ternary

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Annotations in correct order: @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: 1 @TableTest method name(s) read as descriptive titles (no @DisplayName needed)

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description uses text block or is short single-line

assertions.text: Distinct concerns are each covered without cross-multiplying into redundant permutations.
assertions.evidence: Single table with 11 rows targeting age, credit, income concerns without a full combinatorial matrix

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules.
assertions.evidence: 'Senior qualifying score with missing income information | 70 | 610 | | PENDING_REVIEW' duplicates the null-income rule already shown at age 40 (row 8), an unnecessary age×income permutation

assertions.text: Age boundary policy, credit score categorisation, and income status are each covered by minimal scenarios.
assertions.evidence: Rows 1-6 cover age/credit boundaries; rows 7-11 vary income (false, null) at qualifying and non-qualifying scores

assertions.text: Scenario names and @Description text do not restate values the table already shows.
assertions.evidence: @Description states 'approved above a credit score of 650...lower threshold of 600...senior age cutoff is inclusive at 65' — restating thresholds and age cut the rows already carry

assertions.text: The effect of stable income on the outcome is visible from table rows.
assertions.evidence: 'Qualifying score with unstable income | 40 | 700 | false | REJECTED' vs 'Qualifying score with missing income information | 40 | 700 | | PENDING_REVIEW' — same age/score, differing income and decision

assertions.text: The build file (build.gradle) includes org.tabletest:tabletest-junit as a test dependency
assertions.evidence: Build file contains tabletest-junit

assertions.text: Cell values make the rule falsifiable, not merely distinguishable.
assertions.evidence: Decisions vary (REJECTED, APPROVED, PENDING_REVIEW) and none are verbatim copies of input cells, so a fixed-value stub would fail multiple rows

assertions.text: A reader can state the rule from the table alone, without the test method body.
assertions.evidence: Boundary rows like '650 | true | REJECTED' and '651 | true | APPROVED' plus '600'/'601' and '64'/'65' rows make thresholds and age cutoff inferable from the table itself.

assertions.text: Each @DisplayName (or fallback method name) states what the code under test does, not an external fact.
assertions.evidence: void evaluatesLoanApproval(...) — the method name describes the evaluator's action, not a restated domain threshold or policy fact.

assertions.text: The generated test code compiles successfully against the project scaffolding
assertions.evidence: Compilation succeeded

assertions.text: A value the rule's outcome depends on and held constant across rows must be visible as a column or named in title/description.
assertions.evidence: All outcome-relevant values (Age, Credit Score, Stable Income) vary as columns across rows; no hidden constant threshold sits only in the method body, since 650/600/601/651 appear as explicit cell values.
